title: Vector Search Benchmark[eting] - Philipp Krenn, Elastic
talk_summary: Philipp Krenn of Elastic argues that most published benchmarks are 'benchmarketing' — cherry-picked scenarios, stale competitor versions, tuned defaults, and omitted quality metrics — and that the only trustworthy approach is automated, reproducible, self-run benchmarks on your own workload. He describes Elastic's nightly benchmark suite as a defense against the 'slow boiling frog' of gradual performance regression.

takeaways.technique: Nightly regression benchmarks on your own workload
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a wide suite of benchmarks every night against your own system, aggregating the day's changes, to catch gradual performance drift rather than one-off comparisons.

takeaways.technique: Benchmark on your own data, not vendor claims
takeaways.what_they_do: Insist that only benchmarks using your data size, structure, read/write ratio, query shape, latency budget, and hardware are meaningful; vendor benchmarks are not transferable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you will need to do your own benchmarks. Um, don't trust anybody's benchmarks

takeaways.technique: Never benchmark speed without the quality metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Warn that ANN benchmarks often omit precision/recall, so 'faster' can just mean worse results; Elastic itself nearly published benchmarks that forgot the quality attribute.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can produce crap results very quickly um but that is probably not the point of what you do in your benchmarks

takeaways.what_they_do: Benchmarks should be automated and reproducible with all pieces published so anyone can rerun them; Elastic built 'rally' with 'tracks' (data + queries) to tune settings and hardware.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they should definitely be automated and reproducible

takeaways.technique: Mine biased benchmarks for signal instead of discarding them
takeaways.what_they_do: Even a vendor's self-serving benchmark reveals where they think their sweet spot is and what scenarios they optimize for; extract that instead of dismissing it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: even if it's like somebody pro produces a a bad benchmark against a competitor it can tell you like where they think their sweet spot is

takeaways.what_they_do: Small per-change slowdowns (1-2%) are invisible individually but compound; nightly trend tracking is the countermeasure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you make a change today and it makes something 1% slower, you're probably not going to see it
